matches.preview: The model narrowly favours Wrexham at 39% to 32%, with a full 29% for a draw making this a finely balanced contest. Their recent meeting saw Birmingham win 2-0, though they had drawn 1-1 when they previously met. In terms of goals, the model leans toward under 2.5 at 52%, compared to 48% for over.

Derby County's 43% win probability marks them as slight favorites, though the match remains finely balanced with Swansea City at 29% and draws at 28%. Last season produced mixed results for Derby, with a 3-2 away victory at QPR offset by home defeat to Sheffield United and an away loss to Norwich. Swansea closed the campaign on a stronger note, collecting wins away at both QPR and Leicester. The head-to-head record favors Derby, who won 2-0 at home in recent meetings. The goal market suggests a tight affair, with under 2.5 favored at 52%.

Their end-of-season form showed mixed returns: both clubs combined victories with defensive vulnerabilities. Middlesbrough recorded a 5-1 win but struggled in draws, while West Brom showed similar patterns with clean sheet issues across three stalemates. Middlesbrough's head-to-head record is decisive: they have won all five of the recent meetings. The match leans slightly under 2.5 goals at 51% versus 49% over.

Stoke's finish proved particularly punishing, yielding just one draw from six matches. Wolverhampton displayed greater resilience during their late-season run, though three draws could not prevent heavy defeats away to Brighton and Leeds. No previous meetings are recorded between these opponents. The total-goals probability leans modestly toward over 2.5.

Blackburn prevailed 3-1 away in their most recent meeting. The model favours under 2.5 goals at 54%, suggesting relatively restrained goal output overall.

The model leans to under 2.5 goals at 53%, suggesting a tighter contest than the dominant head-to-head wins might indicate.

Historically, Sheffield United dominates this fixture, unbeaten in their last five meetings against Cardiff. The goal outlook leans towards higher scoring, with over 2.5 goals at 54%.

Charlton's slim home advantage in this encounter, the model suggesting a 42% probability of victory, but the match remains finely balanced with Preston at 29%.
